podcasts.title: Building a chip to beat biology | Naveen Rao - Unconventional AI [Tape Out - Ep.001]
podcasts.summary: "We actually build chips every three months. Like we literally tape out a new chip." Naveen Rao has built two AI companies and sold them both: Nervana to Intel and MosaicML to Databricks. His third, Unconventional AI, looks nothing like either of them. His argument is that AI is now limited by energy, so the number that matters is joules per token. Getting there means dropping the von Neumann split between memory and compute and building a machine that is "programmed by weights." To learn fast, his team tapes out a new chip roughly every three months. Their first test chip, a system of coupled oscillators, generated small images at about 900 nanojoules each, against about 50 millijoules on a GPU. Dylan Patel pushes on all of it: - why so many analog chips blew their lead once you count the conversion costs - whether programmability still matters when NVIDIA is king - whether we will stop buying computers and start buying intelligence tokens - how far AI can go in designing chips itself Tape Out is a new SemiAnalysis series: we sit across from the founders building AI hardware and ask the hard questions. podcasts.summary: The human brain remains one of the greatest unsolved mysteries in science. We have roughly 86 billion neurons firing in a way that somehow produces intelligence, and yet the brain is still largely a black box.
